solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Of Mice and Men novel gripping spoon-bender

indicators.note: gripping means holding something inside, so the scrambled letters close around the spoon-bender
novel as an adjective means new or freshly made, so the letters of men are rearranged

parts.note: Uri Geller is the famous spoon-bending entertainer

explanation.surface: A reference to Steinbeck's novel Of Mice and Men oddly featuring a spoon-bending psychic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' scrambles MEN to MNE. The book title tempts as a whole, but only its first two words define; Uri Geller is the famous spoon-bending entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: Murine is the zoological adjective relating to mice and rats, the rodent family Muridae.

clue.text: Hit back and lash out at an officer

indicators.note: back means read backwards, so the word for hit is turned round

parts.note: to hit is to ram

indicators.note: out means disordered or wrong, so the letters of lash are rearranged

explanation.surface: Retaliating and lashing out at a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RAM into MAR, and 'out' scrambles LASH to SHAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A marshal is a high-ranking officer in an army or air force, or a US law officer.

clue.text: European agreement to support port wine region

indicators.note: to support means holding up from below, so in a down clue this piece follows the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
ja is German and Dutch for yes

explanation.surface: Treaty terms supporting a port and its wine-growing area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' works because in a down clue the supporting piece sits below. Rioja is in northern Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: La Rioja is a Spanish area famous for its red wines, which take their name from it.

clue.text: Next store finally discovered in adjacent street

indicators.note: discovered in means found inside, so the letter sits within the other pieces

parts.note: adjacent means near

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A shop found in the neighbouring street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'store' looks like a shop, but only its last letter is used; 'discovered in' then places that letter between the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The one closest to you is the next in line, as in the nearest or next house.

clue.text: One's captivated by a desire for the taste of Pernod, perhaps?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: captivated by means held captive within, so the first piece sits inside the next words

parts.note: a desire is a need
one is I, and the 's stands for is, giving I'S

explanation.surface: Someone yearning for the flavour of the French aperitif Pernod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is read as 'one is', and 'captivated by' places it inside the other words. Pernod is a French anise-flavoured spirit, so the definition is by example, flagged by 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pernod is an anise-flavoured pastis, so its characteristic flavour is that of the aniseed spice.

clue.text: River people in the finale of The Mission with Jeremy Irons ultimately gather in speed …

indicators.note: gather in means take something within, so the letters enclose the speed
the finale of means the last letter of the word
ultimately means at the end, picking the final letter of each of the two words

parts.note: MPH, miles per hour, measures speed

explanation.surface: Jeremy Irons in the film The Mission, at its finale, speeding up a river.
explanation.walkthrough: N and YS (from Mission and Jeremy Irons) gather MPH. Nymphs in myth include naiads, spirits of rivers; the Mission is a 1986 film starring Irons with river scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth naiads were female spirits living in rivers and springs, a class of water nymph.

clue.text: … to bear up De Niro, suffering under the Spanish sun

indicators.note: under means placed below, so in a down clue the scrambled actor comes after the sun

parts.note: sol is Spanish for sun

indicators.note: suffering means in a bad way, so the letters of De Niro are rearranged

explanation.surface: Robert De Niro enduring the heat of the Spanish sun on location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering' scrambles DENIRO to DIERON, and 'under' puts it below SOL in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is to carry on stoically despite difficulty, much as to bear up means.

clue.text: Old seafood sandwiches? I say!

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: sandwiches means holds between, so the shellfish encloses the letter

parts.note: a clam is a shellfish
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone appalled at stale seafood sandwiches, crying out in shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say!' looks like the definition, but I goes inside CLAM and only 'say' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to say something suddenly and loudly, so it is a way of uttering words.

clue.text: Rocky Horror film's winning the French over in the silver screens of Versailles

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
read as films

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the French article is reversed

parts.note: la is French for the

explanation.surface: The Rocky Horror Picture Show winning French audiences in a Versailles cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns LA into AL, and 'Rocky' mixes it with HORROR FILMS; 'winning' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The palace at Versailles has a famous gallery lined with mirrors, poetically screens of silver glass.

clue.text: In the beginning they reposed indivisibly one as the father, spirit and son

indicators.note: In the beginning echoes Genesis and points to the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A biblical-sounding statement of the doctrine of the Holy Trinity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the beginning' takes the first letters of 'they reposed indivisibly one'. The Trinity of Father, Son and Spirit is a group of three.
explanation.definitionFit: Any group of three persons is a threesome, as the Christian Trinity of Father, Son and Spirit is.

clue.text: TimeWarner panic to fix copyright infringement

indicators.note: infringement means encroaching on something, so the copyright symbol trespasses onto the front of the next word

parts.note: panic means alarm
C is the abbreviation for copyright, as in the circled C
to fix in place is to lock

explanation.surface: The media company Time Warner panicking to stop someone breaching its copyright.
explanation.walkthrough: The company name Time Warner is read as 'time warner', something that warns you of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that warns you when a set hour arrives is the bedside clock that rings to wake you.

clue.text: An automotive service is established in the old part of Europe

indicators.note: is established in means set up within, so the motoring club goes inside the word the

parts.note: taken as written
the RAC, Royal Automobile Club, is a British motoring breakdown service

explanation.surface: A car breakdown company opening a branch somewhere in historic Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Thrace is the ancient region now split between Greece, Bulgaria and Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrace was an ancient region in the south-east of the continent, now divided among Greece, Bulgaria and Turkey.

clue.text: Ostentatious ayatollah did a Hajj, setting off late and finishing early

indicators.text: setting off late and finishing early
indicators.note: starting after the first letters and stopping before the last ones means a run is taken from inside these words

explanation.surface: A cleric making a showy pilgrimage to Mecca, leaving late and getting back early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting off late and finishing early' drops the opening letters of 'ayatollah' and the end of 'Hajj', leaving the run in between.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da is an informal British term for pretentious or affected manners, showy and snobbish.

clue.text: Standards have been raised here somewhere in Arizona

definitions.meaning: a standard is a flag, and a pole is where flags are hoisted
a city in northern Arizona near the Grand Canyon

explanation.walkthrough: 'Standards' looks like principles, but here it means flags, which are raised on a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A pole for hoisting flags shares its name with the city of Flagstaff in Arizona.

clue.text: A best friend of Kierkegaard, perhaps?

definitions.text: A best friend of Kierkegaard, perhaps?

parts.words: A best friend of Kierkegaard, perhaps?
parts.note: man's best friend is a dog, and Kierkegaard was an eminent Danish philosopher

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a dog breed (man's best friend) and also describes the Danish philosopher Kierkegaard.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed is a huge dog, man's best friend, and a famous Danish thinker could be called the same.

clue.text: Englishman in Australia gets around a run a ball

indicators.note: gets around means goes round about another piece, so the Englishman encloses the run

parts.note: Pom is Australian slang for an English person
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An English expat in Australia scoring a run off a single delivery in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface (a run off a ball) hides the definition: a ball is a formal dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A prom is a formal school dance, so it is a ball in the dancing sense rather than the sporting one.

clue.text: Gathered to restore the site of Achilles' downfall?

indicators.note: gathered means heard or understood, so the word for restore is taken by ear

parts.note: to restore to health is to heal

explanation.surface: Collected to repair the weak spot of the Greek hero Achilles.
explanation.walkthrough: Achilles was invulnerable except at his heel, where an arrow killed him.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles was dipped as a baby holding him by one foot, leaving the back of it his single vulnerable spot.

clue.text: Harrison Ford's character makes an appearance in the opening of Home Alone

indicators.note: makes signals the next word arriving somewhere
an appearance in means turning up inside, so the short word goes within the other pieces
the opening of picks the first letter of the word

parts.note: alone means solo
taken as written

explanation.surface: Harrison Ford having a cameo in the Christmas comedy Home Alone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Ford in the film Home Alone, but the film title is split: Home gives its opening letter and Alone a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Han Solo is the smuggler pilot that Ford played in the Star Wars films.

clue.text: One filling prescription for future Princess of Wales after Charlie left for first of suitors

indicators.note: left for means one letter quit in favour of another, so a letter is swapped out

parts.note: Lady Diana Spencer, Di Spencer, before marrying Prince Charles
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Diana Spencer ditching Prince Charles to choose the first of her other admirers.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie is both Prince Charles in the surface and C in the radio alphabet; S from 'first of suitors' replaces it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist dispenses medicines, filling the doctor's prescription, so one doing so is a dispenser.

clue.text: Citroën model in photos taken around a well

indicators.note: taken around means wrapped about, so the photos enclose the letter

parts.note: pics is short for pictures or photos
taken as written
so is a filler like well, as in so, what now

explanation.surface: A car seen in photographs taken near a well.
explanation.walkthrough: The Citroën Xsara Picasso was a popular people carrier; 'Citroën model' is the definition, not the artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Citroën sold a compact family car named after the Spanish painter, the Xsara Picasso.

clue.text: Anarche mistakenly omits noun at conclusion of puzzle resulting in a complaint to The Listener

indicators.note: mistakenly means wrongly done, so the letters are rearranged
omits means leaves out, so a letter is dropped
at conclusion of picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A solver's grumble to the Listener crossword about a wrongly spelt answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'omits' drops N from ANARCHE and 'mistakenly' scrambles AARCHE into EARACH; The Listener is a famous Times crossword series, so the complaint is also a solver's.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache in the ear is an ailment, and a listener's ailment puns on the Listener crossword.

clue.text: Source of climate change drastically cut down raincoat production

indicators.note: production means making or working up, so the letters are rearranged
severely cut down means the ending of the word is chopped off

explanation.surface: Air conditioning causing raincoat manufacture to fall sharply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drastically cut down' removes AT from the end of RAINCOAT, and 'production' rearranges RAINCO.
explanation.definitionFit: Air conditioning alters the climate of a room, cooling and drying the indoor atmosphere.

clue.text: More problematic than Gordius, perhaps?

parts.note: Gordius tied the Gordian knot, so he is a tier of knots; also a Guardian setter's pseudonym, making his puzzles tricky

explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits into KNOT TIER, a description of King Gordius, while also meaning more tangled.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotty describes a problem that is intricate and hard to solve, and this is its comparative form.

clue.text: The Prime Minister doesn't take on a media producer

indicators.note: doesn't take means leaving something out, so the word on is removed

parts.note: David Cameron was the UK Prime Minister when this was published
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The PM refusing to agree to an interview with a broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2012 the Prime Minister was David Cameron; drop ON and add A.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that records pictures and film produces the material that the media publish and broadcast.

clue.text: Communist broadcast!?

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Karl Marx was the founding thinker of communism

explanation.surface: A Communist making a startled announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the punctuation itself: '!' and '?' are both punctuation marks.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation and question signs are punctuation symbols, so together they are a pair of them.

clue.text: Lines of speech?

parts.note: lines as in strings or bands, the tissues in the throat that vibrate to make the voice

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines of speech' suggests dialogue in a script; here the lines are the strands in the larynx.
explanation.definitionFit: The folds in the larynx vibrate to produce the voice, so they are the strings or cords behind talking.

clue.text: Infusion of turmeric enhances this?

indicators.note: an infusion is something steeped within, so the run lies inside the following words

explanation.surface: A cookery tip that the yellow spice improves a staple grain dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Infusion of' takes the run across the end of 'turmeric' and the start of 'enhances'; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmeric is commonly added to colour and flavour the grain served with curries, as in pilau.

clue.text: A German encrypted a number?

annotationWithheld.why: A German encrypted a number? (7): EIN inside CODE, where 'encrypted' (in code) is both the container indicator and the source of CODE

clue.text: Almost all the French in disarray

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: tous les is French for all the

explanation.surface: Nearly every French person in a state of chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: TOUS LES is French for 'all the'; 'Almost' drops its last S.
explanation.definitionFit: To tousle hair or clothes is to make them untidy, so it means to put into disarray as a verb.
